reading.body:
Flexential Charlotte - South publishes 2.36 MW of IT capacity across 66,666 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 2.36 MW supports roughly 59 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, the same power supports roughly 236 racks. The arithmetic is an outside assumption, not an operator claim. Either way, 2.36 MW is a small facility by AI infrastructure standards, where meaningful training clusters routinely require tens or hundreds of megawatts.

The certifications tell a clear story about intended workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the campus for financially sensitive and general enterprise trust requirements. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HITRUST qualifies it for regulated healthcare information. ISO 27001 and SSAE 18 signal an auditable information security management framework. Together these certifications point toward compliance-driven enterprise workloads rather than large-scale AI training, which typically prioritizes raw power density over regulatory audit posture.

Among the 19 facilities mapped in North Carolina, only 5 publish a megawatt figure, and this site has read those 5. Flexential Charlotte - South ranks fourth among them, accounting for roughly 4.6 percent of the 51.47 MW total published capacity in the state. North Carolina's published base is itself modest relative to AI-scale deployments, so a fourth-place rank at 2.36 MW places this campus toward the smaller end of a mid-tier state market. For a reader evaluating AI relevance, the campus is better suited to hosting inference endpoints, regulated enterprise AI applications, or data governance workloads than to training foundation models at scale.
